name: Fistula Foundation's repair surgeries (The Life You Can Save, 2025)

missing_data.note: Measured: Fistula Foundation counts the surgeries its partner hospitals perform, and a repair's effect is the clinical closure of the fistula, seen at discharge.

summary: Fistula Foundation pays partner hospitals in Africa and Asia to repair obstetric fistula, an injury from obstructed labour that leaves women leaking urine or faeces. The Life You Can Save estimates $76 per DALY averted from Fistula Foundation's 16,587 surgeries in 2024 at $633 each, counting each woman as spared the fistula's disability for the rest of her life. Our view counts the full cost per surgery including administration, the repairs that fail and the women who would have been repaired anyway; the biggest uncertainties are how many women would otherwise have lived with fistula for life and how often a repair ends the incontinence.

rows.explainer: The sheet's own monitoring row: the cost per surgery with Fistula Foundation's administration and fundraising. 16,587 surgeries at this cost come to 19.7 million dollars, Fistula Foundation's total spending in its 2024 Form 990.

rows.label: Full cost per dollar of the sheet's surgery costs
rows.explainer: The sheet divides by the direct cost of a surgery; a donated dollar also pays Fistula Foundation's administration and fundraising, so our view uses the full cost (the evaluator view keeps the sheet's).

rows.label: Partner hospitals' and governments' own cost per surgery
rows.explainer: Partner hospitals contribute theatres, beds and some staff that Fistula Foundation's grants don't pay for; with credit by share of resources on, their money shares the outcome. Our judgment.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves: the grants pay surgeons, nurses and outreach workers at partner hospitals. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits. Our judgment.

rows.formula: (admin_cost_multiplier * (1 + if($resource_shares, salary_sacrifice, 0)) * cost_per_surgery + if($resource_shares, others_cost_per_surgery, 0)) / cost_per_surgery
rows.explainer: Administration always; with credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay and the hospitals' own money as well.

rows.label: Share of repairs that end the incontinence
rows.explainer: The sheet counts every surgery as a lifelong cure. Surgical series in sub-Saharan Africa close 80% to 95% of fistulas at the first operation, and some women who are closed still leak (residual incontinence); our judgment: 80% (65% to 92%) of repairs end the disability.

rows.label: Share of the women repaired who wouldn't have been repaired anyway
rows.explainer: The sheet credits Fistula Foundation with the whole rest of each woman's life. Some women would have been repaired later through another funder (UNFPA's Campaign to End Fistula, governments, other charities), cutting the years the surgery adds. Our judgment: 75% (50% to 95%) of the counted years.

rows.label: Good of a repair beyond health, as a share of the health gain
rows.explainer: Women with fistula are often left by their husbands and cannot work or take part in community life; repair lets many return to both. The disability weight covers part of this. Our judgment: 10% (0 to 30%) more.

rows.label: DALYs averted per dollar
rows.explainer: The Life You Can Save's DALYs per dollar, after failed repairs and what would have happened anyway, per dollar of the full cost.
